units.function: open from a trend and turn it into a need for a system

original_instantiations: As tools advance and the volume of records surges, stored information turns into a strategic holding, and putting a proper system around it grows steadily more pressing.
Records have become a strategic holding. Building a system to manage and read them matters more with every year.

units.source_excerpt: With the development of technology and the explosive growth of data, data is becoming an important strategic asset, and it is more and more important to establish a suitable system to manage and analyze the data.
units.reusable_pattern: With the development of [the trend], [the subject] is becoming [a status], and it is more and more important to [the response].
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, opening sentence.
stable function: convert a trend into a modelling need.
pattern: With the development of / it is more and more important to.
boundary: the response must be what the paper builds.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the industry.

units.function: announce the model and the two things it delivers

original_instantiations: In this paper we build a model of the factors behind system maturity, showing how to use the records better and how to draw up plans that get the most from them.
We construct a model that exposes the factors and, from them, the plans for using the records fully.

units.source_excerpt: In this paper, we build a model to analyze the factors affecting the maturity, revealing how to make better use of data, and formulate plans to maximize the potential of data assets.
units.reusable_pattern: In this paper, we build a model to [the analysis], revealing how to [the use], and [the plans].
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, second sentence.
stable function: name the model and its two payoffs.
pattern: we build a model to / revealing how to.
boundary: both payoffs must be delivered.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim a payoff the model never gives.

units.function: report one task as a first-then-finally sequence ending in a number

original_instantiations: In the first task: first we screen the indicators from the literature. Then we weight them by combining two methods. Finally we place the result on a five-level scale and report the score.
The task runs in three beats: select the measures, weight them, then read off a level and a number.

units.source_excerpt: In Task1: First, based on the grounded theory, we screen out the indicators. Then we use the combined weighting. Finally, we divide the maturity into five levels and calculate a score of 0.8173.
units.reusable_pattern: In Task [n]: First, [the selection]. Then, [the weighting]. Finally, [the score and the level].
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, one paragraph per task.
stable function: compress a whole task into three beats.
pattern: In Task n: First / Then / Finally.
boundary: the number must be the computed one.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent the score.

units.function: claim a model is valid because two methods agree

original_instantiations: We check the model by setting the simulation against the evaluation and reading the gap between them.
Validity here means the two methods land close to each other.

units.source_excerpt: We verify the validity of the model by comparing the difference between the simulation results and the evaluation model.
units.reusable_pattern: We verify the validity of the model by comparing the difference between [method A] and [method B].
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, task 2.
stable function: define validity as agreement.
pattern: verify the validity of the model by comparing the difference between.
boundary: both methods must be reported.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call agreement with itself a validation.

units.function: turn a uniform error bound into an applicability claim

original_instantiations: The gaps all stay under five percent, which we read as evidence that the model travels across firms of different size.
Every error falls inside the same small band, so the model applies across the range of sizes.

units.source_excerpt: The errors are all smaller than 5%, showing the good applicability of the model to companies of different sizes.
units.reusable_pattern: The errors are all smaller than [the bound], showing the good applicability of the model to [the range].
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, task 4.
stable function: convert a bound into a scope claim.
pattern: all smaller than / showing the good applicability.
boundary: the bound must be the computed one.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not extend applicability past the tested range.

units.function: state the condition under which raw data becomes value

original_instantiations: Only by handling information properly and using it fully can inert records be turned into wealth one can see.
Raw records stay inert unless they are managed and actually used.

units.source_excerpt: Only by properly managing and making full use of information can cold data be transformed into visible wealth.
units.reusable_pattern: Only by [the condition] can [the raw material] be transformed into [the value].
reusable_elements: occurrences: background.
stable function: make the method a precondition of value.
pattern: Only by / can X be transformed into.
boundary: the condition must be what the model supplies.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not promise wealth the model cannot measure.

units.function: draw the paper's task out of the preceding argument

original_instantiations: As a consequence, a sound assessment of a firm's own capability has become the key to improving itself.
So judging its own capability is now the decisive step.

units.source_excerpt: As a consequence, a reasonable assessment of its own data analysis capabilities has become the key for enterprises to improve themselves.
units.reusable_pattern: As a consequence, [the assessment] has become the key for [the actor] to [the goal].
reusable_elements: occurrences: background, closing line.
stable function: land the background on the paper's task.
pattern: has become the key for.
boundary: the task must follow.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call something the key without the preceding argument.

units.function: hand the problem statement to a bulleted list

original_instantiations: Given the background and the constraints in the problem statement, the tasks are the following.
From the statement we take the problems listed below.

units.source_excerpt: Considering the background information and restricted conditions identified in the problem statement, we need to solve the following problems.
units.reusable_pattern: Considering the background information and restricted conditions identified in the problem statement, we need to solve the following problems.
reusable_elements: occurrences: restatement, opening.
stable function: signal a faithful restatement.
pattern: we need to solve the following problems.
boundary: the bullets must match the statement.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add tasks the statement does not contain.

units.function: trace the model back to its earliest source

original_instantiations: The lineage starts with a staged account of how firm systems evolve, first set down at the end of the 1970s, and later models descend from it.
Everything in this family traces back to one early staged description of system growth.

units.source_excerpt: In 1979, Nolan proposed the growth stage model to study the development of enterprise information systems, and it became the prototype of the maturity model.
units.reusable_pattern: In [the year], [the author] proposed [the model] to study [the subject], and it became the prototype of [the descendant].
reusable_elements: occurrences: literature review, opening.
stable function: anchor a lineage.
pattern: proposed / and it became the prototype of.
boundary: the lineage must be accurate.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent the genealogy.

units.function: credit a prior study and mark what it leaves out

original_instantiations: The study brought risk into the maturity model and built a four-level account, but said little about the benefits the technology brings.
It covers the risks and stops there; the gains are left thin.

units.source_excerpt: Kirazli and Moetz introduced risk management into the maturity model and formulated a four-level model, but the advantages are lacking in elaboration.
units.reusable_pattern: [The authors] introduced [the factor] into the model and formulated [the result], but [the gap] are lacking in elaboration.
reusable_elements: occurrences: literature review.
stable function: locate the gap this paper fills.
pattern: but / are lacking in elaboration.
boundary: the gap must be one the paper addresses.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent a gap to justify the paper.

units.function: summarize a literature and name the remaining lack

original_instantiations: Reading across the studies, scholars attend closely to digital management and have done much work on it. Even so, research on digital maturity models is still thin.
The field is active, yet the specific model this paper needs is still scarce.

units.source_excerpt: Through the analysis and summary of many literatures, it can be seen that many scholars pay extensive attention to digital management. Generally speaking, there is still a lack of research on digital maturity models.
units.reusable_pattern: Through the analysis and summary of many literatures, it can be seen that [the consensus]. Generally speaking, there is still a lack of [the gap].
reusable_elements: occurrences: literature review, closing.
stable function: end a review on the opening the paper fills.
pattern: it can be seen that / there is still a lack of.
boundary: the gap must match the contribution.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim a lack the review did not show.

units.function: delegate the whole plan to one figure

original_instantiations: What we do in this problem is set out mainly in the figure.
The figure carries the plan; the prose does not repeat it.

units.source_excerpt: Our work in this problem is mainly shown in the figure 1.
units.reusable_pattern: Our work in this problem is mainly shown in the figure [n].
reusable_elements: occurrences: our work, the only sentence.
stable function: replace a plan section with a diagram.
pattern: is mainly shown in the figure.
boundary: the figure must show the plan.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not point at a figure that shows results.

units.function: frame the assumptions as the foundation of everything after

original_instantiations: We adopt the following assumptions to get the model built. They are the ground everything later stands on.
The assumptions below are not asides; the analysis rests on them.

units.source_excerpt: We made the following assumptions to help us build the model. These constructions are the background and basis for our subsequent analysis.
units.reusable_pattern: We made the following assumptions to help us build the model. These constructions are the background and basis for our subsequent analysis.
reusable_elements: occurrences: assumptions, opening.
stable function: raise assumptions from a list to a foundation.
pattern: the background and basis for our subsequent analysis.
boundary: the analysis must actually use them.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim an unused assumption is foundational.

units.function: justify an assumption by the clarity it buys

original_instantiations: So that the indicator analysis stays clear and controllable, we assume that factors found later are simply part of the maturity still to be improved.
To keep the analysis manageable, anything outside the current list counts as future improvement rather than as a missing variable.

units.source_excerpt: In order to make the indicator analysis clear and controllable, we assume that other indicators found later are not considered by the system and belong to the part of maturity that needs to be improved.
units.reusable_pattern: In order to make [the analysis] clear and controllable, we assume that [the exclusion].
reusable_elements: occurrences: assumptions, first bullet.
stable function: license an omission by tractability.
pattern: in order to make / clear and controllable, we assume.
boundary: the exclusion must be stated.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not hide an omission inside the assumption.

units.function: give an assumption a one-line purpose

original_instantiations: We do this so we can analyse how to use the assets to their fullest.
The assumption exists only to make the optimization possible.

units.source_excerpt: This is done to analyze how to use the data assets to their fullest potential.
units.reusable_pattern: This is done to analyze how to [the goal].
reusable_elements: occurrences: assumptions, final bullet.
stable function: tie one assumption to one later section.
pattern: This is done to analyze how to.
boundary: the later section must exist.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not attach the purpose to the wrong assumption.

units.function: hand the symbols to a table

original_instantiations: The main mathematical symbols of this paper are collected in the table.
Every symbol we rely on is set out below.

units.source_excerpt: The key mathematical notations used in this paper are listed in Table 1.
units.reusable_pattern: The key mathematical notations used in this paper are listed in Table [n].
reusable_elements: occurrences: notation, the only sentence.
stable function: open a symbol table.
pattern: The key mathematical notations used in this paper are listed in.
boundary: the table must follow.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add prose the section does not have.

units.function: reject a naive rule before choosing indicators

original_instantiations: Plenty of factors describe maturity, but a systematic index set is certainly not a case of more being better.
The indicator list should not grow just because it can.

units.source_excerpt: There are many factors that describe the maturity, but the systematic index system is definitely not the bigger the better.
units.reusable_pattern: There are many [factors], but [the system] is definitely not the bigger the better.
reusable_elements: occurrences: indicator section, opening.
stable function: pre-empt the charge of an arbitrary list.
pattern: definitely not the bigger the better.
boundary: a selection principle must follow.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reject size and then keep everything.

units.function: describe grounded theory as climbing from data to system

original_instantiations: With the grounded-theory approach we distil experience out of the raw material and then lift it to the level of a system.
Start from the records, draw out the pattern, and only then build the framework.

units.source_excerpt: Based on the analysis method of grounded theory, we can summarize the experience from the original data, and then rise to the system level.
units.reusable_pattern: Based on [the method], we summarize the experience from the original data, and then rise to the system level.
reusable_elements: occurrences: indicator section.
stable function: justify a bottom-up indicator set.
pattern: summarize the experience from the original data, and then rise to.
boundary: the data must be real.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim grounded theory for a list copied from one source.

units.function: name the three tests an indicator must pass

original_instantiations: We keep the indicators that generalize, that cover the ground, and that overlap little.
Three tests decide what stays: breadth, coverage, and low redundancy.

units.source_excerpt: We extract available indicators and follow the principles of generalization, completeness and little overlap.
units.reusable_pattern: We extract [the candidates] and follow the principles of [the tests].
reusable_elements: occurrences: indicator section.
stable function: state selection criteria before the list.
pattern: follow the principles of.
boundary: the criteria must be applied.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not name a principle and ignore it.

units.function: say what the constructed model both measures and guides

original_instantiations: We build the maturity model on the earlier one, so that it reflects the level in full and gives strategic direction for diagnosis and upgrading.
The model does two jobs at once: it measures the level and it points to what to change.

units.source_excerpt: We develop the maturity model based on the earlier one, which comprehensively reflects the maturity level and provides strategic guidance for diagnosis, transformation and upgrading.
units.reusable_pattern: We develop [the model] based on [the ancestor], which comprehensively reflects [the level] and provides [the guidance].
reusable_elements: occurrences: indicator section.
stable function: bind a model to a predecessor and two jobs.
pattern: which comprehensively reflects / and provides.
boundary: both jobs must be done.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim guidance the model never gives.

units.function: claim a figure resolves a stakeholder's stated worry

original_instantiations: Read against the figure, the model we built answers in full the hiring managers' uncertainty about the people factors.
The diagram settles the question the managers actually asked.

units.source_excerpt: Analyzing the figure, the evaluation model we constructed comprehensively answered the confusion of the recruitment managers about the people factors.
units.reusable_pattern: Analyzing the figure, the model we constructed comprehensively answered the confusion of [the stakeholder] about [the subject].
reusable_elements: occurrences: indicator section, after each diagram.
stable function: tie a diagram to a named audience.
pattern: comprehensively answered the confusion of.
boundary: the stakeholder must have raised the question.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent the stakeholder's question.

units.function: decline to repeat a parallel argument

original_instantiations: The treatment at this level mirrors the earlier one, so the argument is not gone through again.
Same reasoning as before; we do not rehearse it.

units.source_excerpt: The model is similar to the analysis at the employee level, adding two indicators, and the specific analysis process will not be repeated here.
units.reusable_pattern: [The case] is similar to [the earlier one], and the specific analysis process will not be repeated here.
reusable_elements: occurrences: indicator section.
stable function: avoid duplicating a parallel case.
pattern: will not be repeated here.
boundary: the earlier case must truly be parallel.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not skip a case that differs.

units.function: close an indicator survey with the model it produced

original_instantiations: So a fuller and better grounded maturity model is now in place.
The survey ends with the model it was meant to produce.

units.source_excerpt: Therefore, a more comprehensive and scientific data analysis system maturity evaluation model is constructed.
units.reusable_pattern: Therefore, a more comprehensive and scientific [model] is constructed.
reusable_elements: occurrences: indicator section, closing.
stable function: punctuate a construction.
pattern: Therefore, a more comprehensive and scientific / is constructed.
boundary: the comparison must be earned.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim comprehensiveness without the survey.

units.function: read a gap off a set of figures

original_instantiations: Set against the earlier diagrams, the firm falls short at all three levels, so the maturity is not where it should be.
The comparison shows a deficit on every axis.

units.source_excerpt: Comparing the figures, the firm is lacking in all three levels, so the maturity of the data analysis system is not ideal.
units.reusable_pattern: Comparing [the figures], [the subject] is lacking in [the scope], so [the verdict].
reusable_elements: occurrences: indicator section.
stable function: turn a visual comparison into a judgement.
pattern: Comparing the figures / is lacking in / so.
boundary: the figures must support the deficit.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not judge beyond the figures.

units.function: say why the weights matter before computing them

original_instantiations: Fixing the weights is decisive for the evaluation model, because it bears directly on how accurate the result is.
The weights come first, since the whole score depends on them.

units.source_excerpt: The determination of evaluation index weights plays a crucial role, which directly affects the accuracy of model evaluation.
units.reusable_pattern: The determination of [the weights] plays a crucial role, which directly affects [the accuracy].
reusable_elements: occurrences: weighting section, opening.
stable function: justify a weighting section.
pattern: plays a crucial role, which directly affects.
boundary: the consequence must be real.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not inflate the role.

units.function: defend a hybrid method by what it joins

original_instantiations: One method is objective and the other subjective; joining them gives an evaluation that raises both the rationality and the correctness of the result.
The combination takes the strengths of each and improves the assessment on both counts.

units.source_excerpt: This is a comprehensive evaluation method that combines subjective and objective and integrates various methods, which can effectively improve the rationality and correctness of evaluation.
units.reusable_pattern: This is a comprehensive evaluation method that combines [kind A] and [kind B], which can effectively improve [the payoff].
reusable_elements: occurrences: weighting section.
stable function: defend a hybrid on principle.
pattern: combines subjective and objective / which can effectively improve.
boundary: both kinds must be used.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim improvement without the combination.

units.function: derive a formula from a named concept

original_instantiations: From the notion of self-information and entropy, the information entropy of each indicator follows.
The concept hands us the formula directly.

units.source_excerpt: According to the concept of self-information and entropy in information theory, the information entropy of each evaluation indicator can be calculated, and thus.
units.reusable_pattern: According to the concept of [the idea] in [the field], [the quantity] can be calculated, and thus [the formula].
reusable_elements: occurrences: weighting section.
stable function: attach a formula to its source concept.
pattern: According to the concept of / and thus.
boundary: the formula must implement the concept.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not cite a field the formula does not use.

units.function: motivate a check before presenting it

original_instantiations: To be sure the judgement matrix is accurate, we run a consistency check on it.
Accuracy is not assumed; it is tested.

units.source_excerpt: In order to ensure the accuracy of the judgment matrix, we perform a consistency check on the judgment matrix.
units.reusable_pattern: In order to ensure the accuracy of [the object], we perform [the check].
reusable_elements: occurrences: weighting section.
stable function: announce a validation step.
pattern: In order to ensure the accuracy of / we perform.
boundary: the check must be carried out.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not announce a check that is never computed.

units.function: state the pass rule for a test

original_instantiations: If the computed ratio falls below one tenth, the matrix passes the consistency test.
Below the threshold, the matrix is accepted.

units.source_excerpt: If calculated CR is less than 0.1, then the judgment matrix can pass the consistency test.
units.reusable_pattern: If calculated [the statistic] is less than [the threshold], then [the object] can pass the [test].
reusable_elements: occurrences: weighting section.
stable function: give a test its decision rule.
pattern: If calculated / is less than / then can pass.
boundary: the threshold must be the conventional one.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not lower the threshold silently.

units.function: turn an analogy into an equation

original_instantiations: The gap between the two weights ought to match the gap between their two coefficients, and the coefficients sum to one. Hence the system below.
We set the coefficients so their split mirrors the split of the weights.

units.source_excerpt: The difference between the subjective weight and the objective weight should be the same as the difference between the coefficients. As a result.
units.reusable_pattern: The difference between [A] and [B] should be the same as the difference between [C] and [D]. As a result [the equation].
reusable_elements: occurrences: weighting section.
stable function: motivate a mixing rule.
pattern: should be the same as the difference between / As a result.
boundary: the equation must express the analogy.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not assert the analogy without solving it.

units.function: borrow a method's idea for one step

original_instantiations: Taking the idea of a ranking method, we rescale the score and bring in a membership function.
We borrow only the rescaling step, not the whole method.

units.source_excerpt: Based on the idea of the Topsis method, we process and analyze the score and introduce a membership function.
units.reusable_pattern: Based on the idea of [the method], we [the adaptation] and introduce [the device].
reusable_elements: occurrences: solution section.
stable function: mark a partial borrowing.
pattern: Based on the idea of / we introduce.
boundary: do not claim the whole method was used.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not upgrade a borrowed idea into a full method.

units.function: read a score as good but not finished

original_instantiations: The system sits in a fairly mature band, maturity is relatively high, and even so some room remains to go further.
High, but not at the ceiling.

units.source_excerpt: The existing system is in a relatively mature range, with a relatively high degree of maturity, and there is still room for improvement to a certain extent.
units.reusable_pattern: [The subject] is in a relatively [level] range, and there is still room for improvement to a certain extent.
reusable_elements: occurrences: solution section.
stable function: keep a good result from sounding final.
pattern: there is still room for improvement to a certain extent.
boundary: the next section must use the room.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim room the scale does not allow.

units.function: reframe a vague goal as a maximization

original_instantiations: To get the most from the system we take up a planning model and recast the aim as maximizing the score.
The loose goal becomes a number to push up.

units.source_excerpt: In order to maximize the potential, consider adopting the goal planning model, to convert the goal to maximize the score of the data analysis system.
units.reusable_pattern: In order to [the loose goal], consider adopting [the model], to convert the goal to maximize [the score].
reusable_elements: occurrences: optimization section, opening.
stable function: turn a slogan into an objective.
pattern: convert the goal to maximize.
boundary: the objective must be the one optimized.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not maximize a quantity the model does not own.

units.function: open an optimization as numbered steps

original_instantiations: Step one: settle the decision variables. We take the size of each improvement as the variable and assume the cost of a one-percent gain is known.
First fix what is being chosen, then write the objective.

units.source_excerpt: Step 1: Determination of decision variables. This paper assumes that the cost required to increase different indicators by 1% is known, and determines the size of the improvement as a decision variable.
units.reusable_pattern: Step [n]: [the label]. This paper assumes that [the given], and determines [the variable].
reusable_elements: occurrences: optimization section.
stable function: make an optimization auditable as steps.
pattern: Step n: Determination of.
boundary: the steps must be in order.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not number steps that are not sequential.

units.function: derive a constraint from the direction of improvement

original_instantiations: Because the changes are meant to unlock potential, the existing indicators can only stay or rise. Hence the sign constraint.
Improvement never runs backward, so every change is non-negative.

units.source_excerpt: Due to the improvement of the indicators to play the potential of the system, the existing indicators can only be maintained or improved, in consequence.
units.reusable_pattern: Due to [the purpose], [the restriction], in consequence [the constraint].
reusable_elements: occurrences: optimization section.
stable function: verbalize a constraint before its formula.
pattern: in consequence.
boundary: the formula must match the words.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a constraint the formula lacks.

units.function: claim a method works at two scales at once

original_instantiations: Studying the system this way allows both a broad treatment that folds in every factor and a close treatment that starts from a single one.
The method zooms out and zooms in.

units.source_excerpt: It can not only conduct comprehensive macro research by integrating all factors, but also conduct micro analysis starting from a certain influencing factor.
units.reusable_pattern: It can not only [the broad use] but also [the narrow use].
reusable_elements: occurrences: system dynamics section.
stable function: sell a method on its range.
pattern: can not only / but also.
boundary: both uses must appear.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the narrow use if only the broad one is shown.

units.function: read an error under a threshold as validation

original_instantiations: The error comes out at 7.6 percent, under the ten percent line, which counts as a high-precision result and supports the model.
Below the threshold, so the model holds.

units.source_excerpt: The value is 7.6%, lower than 10%, which is high precision, verifying the validity and stability of the model.
units.reusable_pattern: The value is [the result], lower than [the threshold], which is [the reading], verifying [the claim].
reusable_elements: occurrences: solution section.
stable function: cash a number against a cutoff.
pattern: lower than / which is / verifying.
boundary: the threshold must be stated.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat a self-comparison as external validation.

units.function: convert the largest gap into an investment recommendation

original_instantiations: The widest gap sits in teamwork and technical management. Put the limited funds there and the records yield the most.
Spend where the gap is largest.

units.source_excerpt: The biggest difference is the level of teamwork and technical management. If the limited capital is invested in these two aspects, the greatest potential of data assets can be exerted.
units.reusable_pattern: The biggest difference is [the factor]. If the limited capital is invested in [it], the greatest potential can be exerted.
reusable_elements: occurrences: solution section.
stable function: turn a comparison into spending advice.
pattern: If the limited capital is invested in / the greatest potential can be exerted.
boundary: the factor must be the largest gap.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not recommend spending on a small gap.

units.function: assign a task to one named algorithm

original_instantiations: We set the standard for judging effectiveness, and the association rules carry most of the work.
The job falls mainly to one algorithm.

units.source_excerpt: Formulate the standard to measure the effectiveness, which is mainly solved by the association algorithm based on the association relationship.
units.reusable_pattern: [The task], which is mainly solved by [the algorithm].
reusable_elements: occurrences: algorithm section, opening.
stable function: name the workhorse method.
pattern: which is mainly solved by.
boundary: the algorithm must be the one used.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not credit an algorithm that only appears in a diagram.

units.function: state the two cutoffs that drive the mining

original_instantiations: Support and confidence are governed by cutoffs. We fix the minimum support at one fifth and the minimum confidence at three fifths.
Two numbers decide which rules survive.

units.source_excerpt: The support and confidence are measured by setting thresholds. The minimum support threshold is set to 20%, and the minimum confidence threshold is 60%.
units.reusable_pattern: [The measures] are measured by setting thresholds. The minimum [measure] is set to [the value].
reusable_elements: occurrences: algorithm section.
stable function: expose the tuning choices.
pattern: are measured by setting thresholds / is set to.
boundary: both values must appear.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not hide a threshold.

units.function: read one rule as evidence for a level

original_instantiations: The rules show that the top people band carries very high support and confidence for the top maturity band, which means the system reaches its best only once the people side does.
When the people measure hits its top band, the whole system follows.

units.source_excerpt: The rules indicate that the fourth-level people level has extremely high support and confidence for the fifth-level maturity, indicating that when the people level reaches the fourth level, the system can reach a higher level.
units.reusable_pattern: [The rules] indicate that [the level] has extremely high [statistics] for [the target], indicating that [the conclusion].
reusable_elements: occurrences: results, per rule group.
stable function: translate a rule into advice.
pattern: indicate that / has extremely high / indicating that.
boundary: the statistics must be the mined ones.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not upgrade a rule past its confidence.

units.function: collapse every rule into one operating standard

original_instantiations: Taken across every rule, effectiveness is satisfactory once people and process hit the fourth band and technology hits the third or fourth.
All the rules converge on one triple of levels.

units.source_excerpt: Comprehensive analysis of all rules, when the people reaches the fourth level, the technology the third or fourth, and the process the fourth, the effectiveness is fine.
units.reusable_pattern: Comprehensive analysis of all [rules], when [the conditions], [the verdict].
reusable_elements: occurrences: results, closing.
stable function: end a rule list with one standard.
pattern: Comprehensive analysis of all / when / the verdict.
boundary: the standard must follow from the rules.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a condition no rule supports.

units.function: rename a task as a test of the model

original_instantiations: Asking whether the model works for bigger or smaller firms is really a test of the model itself.
The transfer question doubles as a sensitivity test.

units.source_excerpt: Analyzing whether our model can be used for larger or smaller companies, which is essentially a test of the model.
units.reusable_pattern: Analyzing whether [the transfer], which is essentially a test of [the model].
reusable_elements: occurrences: sensitivity section, opening.
stable function: recast an application as a test.
pattern: which is essentially a test of.
boundary: the test must be performed.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call an untested transfer a test.

units.function: argue that scale changes which indicator matters

original_instantiations: A larger firm holds more records and leans harder on stability and speed; a smaller one leans on individual ability. So the emphasis shifts with scale.
Size changes what the evaluation should reward.

units.source_excerpt: Larger companies have more data and higher requirements for stability and response speed; smaller ones have higher requirements for personal ability. Therefore, companies of different scales have different emphases.
units.reusable_pattern: [The large case]; [the small case]. Therefore, [subjects] of different scales have different emphases.
reusable_elements: occurrences: sensitivity section.
stable function: motivate a reweighting.
pattern: Therefore / have different emphases.
boundary: both cases must be stated.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not assert the shift without the contrast.

units.function: read a flat error curve as applicability

original_instantiations: As the relative size changes, the gap between evaluation and simulation stays small and never rises above five percent, which speaks to the model's reach.
The error barely moves, and that is the evidence.

units.source_excerpt: With the change of the relative size, the error is small, and both remain below 5%, which shows the good applicability of the model to companies of different sizes.
units.reusable_pattern: With the change of [the parameter], [the error] is small and both remain below [the bound], which shows [the claim].
reusable_elements: occurrences: sensitivity section.
stable function: convert a flat curve into a scope claim.
pattern: both remain below / which shows the good applicability.
boundary: the bound must be the observed one.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not extend the claim past the sizes tested.

units.function: open a generality claim with its reasons

original_instantiations: What makes the model travel is the following.
The generality rests on two points, set out below.

units.source_excerpt: The universality of the system lies in.
units.reusable_pattern: The universality of [the model] lies in [the reasons].
reusable_elements: occurrences: promotion section.
stable function: introduce a transfer argument.
pattern: The universality of / lies in.
boundary: the reasons must follow.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not assert universality without the reasons.

units.function: defend transfer by saying what the model avoids

original_instantiations: The model is not built on the records one particular firm generates. It evaluates from the angles of people, tools and procedures, which every systematic assessment shares.
By staying above the specific data, the model moves to other firms.

units.source_excerpt: The model is not directly based on the data generated by the specific company, but conducts evaluation from the perspectives of people, technology and process, thus ensuring the model can be directly transferred.
units.reusable_pattern: [The model] is not directly based on [the specific data], but [the general angles], thus ensuring [the transfer].
reusable_elements: occurrences: promotion section.
stable function: argue transfer from abstraction.
pattern: not directly based on / but / thus ensuring.
boundary: the angles must really be shared.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim transfer to a domain that lacks the angles.

units.function: list what the client gains if others adopt the model

original_instantiations: If the firm's customers adopt the model too, the gains are the following.
Wider adoption pays the firm in three ways.

units.source_excerpt: If their customers also use the model, there will be the following benefits.
units.reusable_pattern: If [the wider adoption], there will be the following benefits.
reusable_elements: occurrences: promotion section.
stable function: open a benefits list.
pattern: there will be the following benefits.
boundary: the benefits must be specific.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not list benefits the model cannot produce.

units.function: credit robustness to the pairing of two methods

original_instantiations: We simulate to get the data and give the strategy in words; alongside that, the linear program quantifies where to improve. Pairing the two strengthens the model.
Qualitative and quantitative together make the result sturdier.

units.source_excerpt: We use simulation to obtain data and qualitatively give improvement strategies; at the same time, combined with linear programming, we quantitatively analyze the focus. The combination of the two methods enhances the robustness of the model.
units.reusable_pattern: We use [method A] to [the qualitative job]; at the same time [method B] [the quantitative job]. The combination of the two enhances the robustness.
reusable_elements: occurrences: strengths.
stable function: defend a two-method design.
pattern: at the same time / The combination of the two enhances the robustness.
boundary: both methods must be present.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim robustness from one method.

units.function: claim a model inherits theory and adds to it

original_instantiations: Most of the models start from an existing theory or improve on it for this problem, so they stay grounded and still add something.
Built on prior work, adapted to the case: both at once.

units.source_excerpt: Most of our models are based on innovative ideas or improvements based on the original theory and the problem, making our models both theoretical and innovative.
units.reusable_pattern: Most of our models are based on [the basis], making our models both [quality A] and [quality B].
reusable_elements: occurrences: strengths, closing bullet.
stable function: claim dual virtue.
pattern: making our models both / and.
boundary: both qualities must be defensible.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim innovation for an unmodified import.

units.function: concede a deeper analysis and blame the page limit

original_instantiations: We could have gone deeper into how the three levels relate, but the page limit stops us for now.
The relation deserves more, and there is no room left.

units.source_excerpt: We could have analyzed the relationship between the three levels in more depth, but due to space limitations, our work can only do this for the time being.
units.reusable_pattern: We could have [the deeper analysis], but due to space limitations, our work can only do this for the time being.
reusable_elements: occurrences: weaknesses.
stable function: bound the work by length.
pattern: We could have / but due to space limitations.
boundary: the missed analysis must be real.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not blame space for a gap of substance.

units.function: state what the evidence allows and what it rules out

original_instantiations: With no real numerical reference available, we can judge accuracy only by setting simulation against evaluation, and we cannot test it on actual company data.
The check is internal. An external one is out of reach.

units.source_excerpt: Due to the lack of actual numerical reference, we can only observe the accuracy from the comparison of simulation and evaluation, but cannot measure the accuracy through actual company data.
units.reusable_pattern: Due to the lack of [the data], we can only [the available check], but cannot [the unavailable one].
reusable_elements: occurrences: weaknesses.
stable function: bound a validation honestly.
pattern: Due to the lack of / we can only / but cannot.
boundary: the available check must be the one performed.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not imply the unavailable check was done.

units.function: open a letter by naming who asked and for what

original_instantiations: We are the researchers the firm asked to judge how mature its system is.
The firm brought us in to assess the system.

units.source_excerpt: We are the researchers invited by the company to assess the maturity of its system.
units.reusable_pattern: We are the [role] invited by [the client] to [the task].
reusable_elements: occurrences: letter, opening.
stable function: locate the writers.
pattern: We are the / invited by / to.
boundary: the invitation must be real.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent the invitation.

units.function: tell the reader why the system matters to them

original_instantiations: Only a genuinely mature system can put all this daily information to full use, catch customers' problems in time, and save their time.
The reader's own time depends on the system being mature.

units.source_excerpt: Only with a sufficiently mature data analysis system can these data be fully utilized, understand the problems and needs of customers in a timely manner, and save your precious time.
units.reusable_pattern: Only with [the condition] can [the data] be fully utilized and [the benefit to the reader].
reusable_elements: occurrences: letter.
stable function: connect the model to the reader's interest.
pattern: Only with / can / be fully utilized.
boundary: the benefit must be plausible.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not promise a benefit the model cannot touch.

units.function: read a score as proof and soften it with one gap

original_instantiations: The system scored 0.8173 out of one, which shows it is fairly mature, and it also bears out the firm's strength, with only a small shortfall in talent management and teamwork.
The number supports the firm and names the two places it falls short.

units.source_excerpt: The system finally got a score of 0.8173, which proves that it is at a relatively mature level. It also confirms the undoubted strength, only slightly lacking in talent management and teamwork.
units.reusable_pattern: [The subject] got a score of [the value], which proves that [the level]. It also confirms [the strength], only slightly lacking in [the gap].
reusable_elements: occurrences: letter.
stable function: deliver a result without overselling it.
pattern: which proves that / It also confirms / only slightly lacking in.
boundary: the gap must be the one found.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not omit the gap.

units.function: close by transferring the benefit to the reader

original_instantiations: Since the system rests on people, tools and procedures, it fits ports large and small and other trades too. Used on your own operation, it should deepen your grasp of it and your confidence in the firm, toward a result that benefits both sides.
The same model serves you, and trust follows.

units.source_excerpt: Because our evaluation system is based on people, technology and process, it is also applicable to all enterprises. I believe that using our evaluation system, you can have a deeper understanding of yourself. You will also have more trust, to achieve mutual benefit and win-win.
units.reusable_pattern: Because [the basis], it is also applicable to [the range]. I believe that using [it], you can [the gain]. You will also have more trust, to achieve [the shared outcome].
reusable_elements: occurrences: letter, closing.
stable function: end on the reader's benefit.
pattern: I believe that using / you will also have more trust.
boundary: the basis must support the range.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not promise trust the result does not earn.

units.function: close with twelve numbered sources mixing journals and standards

original_instantiations: Twelve numbered sources, from a capability-maturity comparison to an ISO 9001 case study.
A numbered list mixing journals, conference papers and a standard.

units.source_excerpt: References [1] to [12], from Paulk's comparison of ISO 9001 and the capability maturity model to an ISO 9001 case study.
units.reusable_pattern: A numbered list of twelve sources spanning journals, conference proceedings and a management standard.
reusable_elements: occurrences: references.
stable function: none reusable; the mix is this paper's own.
pattern: none.
boundary: not a move to imitate.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not copy the reference list.
